For example, under the proposed regulations a truck moving from a point in the New Jersey portion of the zone to New York City would be unable to make a stop-off at any other point in New Jersey which is not within the commercial zone of the origin point. Another truck would be needed to make the second delivery. Several other shippers and shipper associations also urge that the exemption be extended to the points in New Jersey and in Westchester and Nassau Counties which are within the extended zone.
Interested parties located in several port cities requested that their cities be given special consideration. The San Francisco Port Commission and maritime interests point out that San Francisco's proposed new commercial zone which would be determined according to the consolidated government rule, would be smaller than its present zone and smaller than the zone would be if the population-mileage formula were applied to San Francisco. They propose that San Francisco and Oakland be treated as twin cities and be given a single commercial zone by applying the population-mileage formula to their combined populations. In support of this request they point out that the two cities share a single mass transportation system and jointly participate in planning their metropolitan area. They request that if the Commission does not see fit to treat San Francisco and Oakland as twin cities, that San Francisco be exempted from the consolidated governments rule and be allowed to define its commercial zone according to the proposed population-mileage formula.
